text.p: Diversified manufacturer Pacific Dunlop Ltd said on Friday it was considering several growth initiatives, both inside and outside Australia.
"Preparatory work is already under way on growth initiatives for the future. Several projects are being examined, both inside and outside Australia," chairman John Gough told the annual meeting.
He did not give details but said any decision to go ahead with new projects would be made only if they met the goal of increased, sustainable returns to shareholders.

The group is considering investments of the size and type of its A$75 million purchase of the Perry medical glove business last year, Pacific Dunlop managing director Rod Chadwick told reporters after the meeting.
"I think rather than one investment it may well be a series of smaller investments. They have tended to be more successful in the past," he said.
Chadwick said any acquisitions were likely to be "add-on" purchases which enhanced its existing businesses and that Asia offered further investment opportunities.
"If we are not going to diversify...then we will need to grow product lines that we have internationally and I think that in all those emerging economies there are opportunities for us," he said.
